notes.R1: Its test makes R-step's own call, consecutive_groups([2, 4, 6, 10, 12], step=2), and checks only that step is accepted (no TypeError), which is the first part of R-step; it asserts no grouping result.
notes.R2: Asserts R-step's example ([2, 4, 6, 10, 12] with step=2 gives [2, 4, 6] and [10, 12]) and generalises only to positive integer steps, so it checks nothing about negative steps or step=0.
notes.R3: Directly asserts that calls without step match the base implementation (R-default-unchanged); its wording covers every call that omits step and its observable runs the existing consecutive_groups tests, which pass ordering positionally, so it also partly checks R-positional-ordering, while its list(g) comparisons do not check R-lazy.
